rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause, relocation assistance, buyouts, retaliation)
rules.requirement: A landlord may end a covered tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For no-fault terminations the landlord must pay (or waive) 2 months' rent as relocation assistance, or 3 months if the tenant is 62+ or disabled, and give 30/60 days' notice. Buyout agreements are regulated and retaliation is prohibited.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance: 2 months' rent (3 months if senior 62+/disabled) for no-fault terminations
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
rules.effective_date_note: Division as retitled/expanded by O-21647 N.S., effective 2023-06-24; amended by O-21769 N.S., effective 2024-03-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies longer than 30 days (not fixed terms of 3 months or less) in residential rental property in San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, short-term rentals, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8), mobilehomes under the MRL, nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities, dormitories, owner-occupied single-family residence or duplex, housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, and separately alienable property (e.g. condos) of non-REIT/corporate landlords with written notice.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief and damages including punitive; at least 3x actual economic damages for wrongful eviction; at least 3x relocation assistance owed; attorney's fees; noncompliant notices are void; City enforcement.
rules.interaction: Rights are in addition to state and federal rights; consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 but provides greater relocation assistance.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property (e.g. condos) owned by non-corporate landlord with written notice
dormitories, care facilities, nonprofit transitional housing

rules.review_note: D077 (Legal Aid fact sheet, Sept 2023) corroborates the June 24, 2023 effective date and 2/3-month relocation schedule.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data to set rents or occupancy levels, and vendors may not sell or license such software to landlords. Tenants can sue for injunctions, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees; each month and each property is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11
Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.effective_date_note: Official text in D076 is a draft with blank passage date (effective 30th day after final passage); Morgan Lewis alert (D002/D037) states effective June 2025. Exact day not available.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Software publishing reports from aggregated historical nonpublic data over 90 days old or public information that does not recommend future rents; software used to set rents/income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: Injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and attorney's fees.

unverifiable_exemptions: software used for affordable housing program rent/income limits

rules.review_note: Enactment is confirmed only by secondary sources (D002, D037); D076 is the draft ordinance text.

rules.title: San Diego prohibition of discrimination based on a tenant's source of income
rules.requirement: San Diego has a municipal division prohibiting discrimination based on a tenant's source of income (the text could not be read). Check the code division for details.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 8
rules.quoted_span: Section 8 means residential rental property in which the tenant receives tenant-based housing assistance under Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937,
rules.conflict_note: Unverified: inferred from the title of link-only source D075. Quoted span is from D073 (defines Section 8 voucher) and only generally supports the proposition.
rules.review_note: Section numbers, effective date, and requirements not available.

parsed.notes: Merged c64/c101 (just cause) and c65/c79/c92 (algorithmic). Added unverified source-of-income rule from link-only D075. No documents addressed San Diego rent increase limits, security deposits or application fees, so no findings were made for those.
